preamble.summary: Deuteronomy 1 opens Moses' great valedictory address from the plains of Moab. The chapter is well attested at Qumran. 4QDeutʰ (4Q35) is the most extensive Cave 4 manuscript of Deuteronomy 1–9 and preserves substantial portions; 4QDeutᶜ, 1QDeutᵃ, and 11QDeut also attest fragments. The preserved text tracks the MT closely, with only orthographic variation (plene vs. defective spellings).
preamble.notable_variants: No significant theological or content variants. The 4Q witnesses use plene spelling more frequently than the MT (e.g., כול for כל, רואש for ראש), reflecting Second Temple Hebrew orthographic conventions, but the consonantal text and meaning are identical.
preamble.scroll_condition: Fragmentary but clear where preserved. 4QDeutʰ provides the most continuous text; readings of vv. 22–25 and 9–13 are well preserved.

variant_notes: The opening superscription is preserved in 4QDeutʰ; reads identically to the MT.
1QDeutᵃ preserves part of the spy-mission account (vv. 22–25). Tracks MT; minor orthographic plene spelling.
Tracks MT. The good-land report ("It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us") is preserved verbatim.
